description: Two-panel Thermo-Calc (TCFE 12) equilibrium calculation for the experimental Fe–9Mn–5Al–0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel; both panels plot phase/composition data against Temperature /°C. (a) "Amount of all phases /mol" (0.0–1.0) versus ~500–1600 °C, legend FCC_A1 (black), BCC_A2 (red), CEMENTITE (blue), LIQUID (green): FCC_A1 rises from about 0.1 at 500 °C to a broad maximum just above the 0.9 gridline near 970 °C, BCC_A2 falls to a minimum near the 0.1 gridline at that same temperature, the CEMENTITE curve ends where an arrow labelled "617 °C" points, and LIQUID appears near 1390 °C, reaching 1.0 above ~1450 °C. (b) dual-axis partitioning plot, left axis "Mass fraction/%" (0–20) for Mn and Al, right axis "Mass fraction of C/%" (0.0–1.0) for C, versus ~500–1400 °C, with six entries: Mn, Al and C in ferrite (solid lines) and in austenite (dashed lines). Mn in austenite shows a sharp peak near 600 °C; C in austenite peaks near 0.65 at ~620 °C, falls to a minimum around 1000 °C, then rises; Al in ferrite stays nearly flat at ~4.5–5 % while Al in austenite declines; Mn and C in ferrite increase toward 1400 °C. Together the panels define the δ-ferrite + austenite dual-phase window and justify the chosen quenching/intercritical annealing temperatures.

subfigures.description: Thermo-Calc phase-fraction vs temperature plot: y-axis "Amount of all phases /mol" (0.0–1.0), x-axis Temperature /°C (~500–1600). Legend: FCC_A1 (black), BCC_A2 (red), CEMENTITE (blue), LIQUID (green). FCC_A1 rises to a maximum just above the 0.9 gridline near 970 °C while BCC_A2 drops to a minimum near the 0.1 gridline; an arrow labelled "617 °C" marks where the CEMENTITE curve terminates; LIQUID appears near 1390 °C and climbs to 1.0 above ~1450 °C.

Dual-axis mass-fraction plot vs Temperature /°C (~500–1400). Left axis "Mass fraction/%" 0–20 (Mn, Al); right axis "Mass fraction of C/%" 0.0–1.0 (C). Legend: Mn in ferrite (solid red), Mn in austenite (dashed red), Al in ferrite (solid blue), Al in austenite (dashed blue), C in ferrite (solid black), C in austenite (dashed black). Dashed red Mn-in-austenite shows a sharp maximum near 600 °C; dashed black C-in-austenite peaks near 0.65 at ~620 °C, decreases to a minimum around 1000 °C then rises again; Al in ferrite is nearly flat ~4.5–5 %, Al in austenite declines; Mn and C in ferrite rise steadily toward 1400 °C.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a calculated phase-fraction plot with y-axis "Amount of all phases /mol" spanning 0.0–1.0 and x-axis "Temperature /°C" spanning roughly 500–1600 °C.
The legend of (a) contains four phases: FCC_A1, BCC_A2, CEMENTITE and LIQUID.

In (a) the FCC_A1 curve peaks just above the 0.9 gridline between 900 and 1000 °C while the BCC_A2 curve simultaneously reaches its minimum near the 0.1 gridline, producing a crossing dual-phase region.
An arrow labelled "617 °C" in panel (a) points to the low-temperature end of the blue CEMENTITE curve, where that phase terminates.
The green LIQUID curve of (a) first appears near 1390 °C and rises to 1.0 above about 1450 °C.
Panel (b) uses two y-axes: "Mass fraction/%" (0–20) on the left for Mn and Al, and "Mass fraction of C/%" (0.0–1.0) on the right for carbon, with Temperature /°C on the x-axis.
In (b) the dashed red "Mn in austenite" curve shows a sharp maximum near 600 °C close to the 20 % top of the left axis, then decreases steeply to a plateau at lower values beyond 800 °C.
The dashed black "C in austenite" curve (right axis) peaks near 0.65 at about 620 °C, decreases to a minimum around 1000 °C and then increases again toward 1400 °C.
In (b) Al in ferrite (solid blue) remains nearly flat at roughly 4.5–5 % across the whole temperature range, whereas Al in austenite (dashed blue) declines gradually from about 4.6 % to about 3 %.

The caption states that (a) is the phase fraction of the experimental steel calculated by Thermo-Calc software and (b) the mass fraction of the corresponding ferrite and austenite composition as a function of temperature.

The citing text states that δ-ferrite (δ-F, BCC, A2) begins to precipitate from the liquid (L) at about 1485 °C and that austenite (A, FCC_A1) forms at about 1390 °C by the peritectic reaction δ-F + L → A.
The citing text states that the austenite fraction reaches a maximum of about 91.4 % and δ-ferrite a minimum of about 8.6 % at around 970 °C.
The citing text states the A1 temperature (cementite precipitation point) is about 617 °C and that 620 °C, 680 °C, 740 °C and 800 °C were selected as intercritical annealing temperatures.

The citing text states that the addition of 4.6 % Al expands the δ-ferrite phase region, so the steel cannot be completely austenitized and a dual-phase ferrite + austenite zone spans a considerable temperature range; 1050 °C was selected as the quenching temperature.

unreadable_items: Exact numeric values of individual curve points in both panels are not printed; only gridlines and the "617 °C" annotation are readable.
